Policy says to setup a local environment instead of pen-testing production wherever possible; if production must be tested, limit data access/modification to bare minimum. Bounties are DOUBLED if reported before the bug is released to users (pre-release disclosure bonus). CVSS < 4.0 vulnerabilities generally not in scope unless combinable for higher impact. Third-party S3 buckets/cloud infra with 'WordPress' in the name are explicitly called out as NOT owned by WordPress. Plugin vulnerabilities for plugins not specifically listed as in-scope assets should be reported to the Plugin Review team, not here. safe_harbor defaulted to false — policy text references HackerOne's disclosure guidelines but does not include an explicit safe-harbor clause; human should verify. bucket_download_allowed defaulted to false (safe default; not addressed in policy). requires_ownership_proof defaulted to true (safe default; not addressed in policy). cve_age_min_days defaulted to 30 (safe default; not addressed in policy).

raw_policy_excerpt:
WordPress is an open-source publishing platform. Our HackerOne program covers the Core software, as well as a variety of related projects and infrastructure.

Our most critical targets are:
* WordPress Core software, API, and website.
* Gutenberg software and Classic Editor software.
* WP-CLI software and website.
* BuddyPress software and website.
* bbPress software and website.
* GlotPress software (but not the website).
* WordCamp.org website.

All bounties are doubled if they're reported before the bug is released to users.

Please note that WordPress.com is a separate entity from the main WordPress open source project. Please report vulnerabilities for WordPress.com or the WordPress mobile apps through Automattic's HackerOne page.

## Qualifying Vulnerabilities
Any reproducible vulnerability that has a severe effect on the security or privacy of our users is likely to be in scope. Common examples include XSS, CSRF, SSRF, RCE, SQLi, and privilege escalation.

We generally aren't interested in: Any vulnerability with a CVSS 3 score lower than 4.0 (unless combinable); Brute force, DoS, phishing, text injection, or social engineering; Output from automated scans without manual PoC; Theoretical vulnerabilities without significant PoC.

## Guidelines
* Please setup a local environment instead whenever possible.
* If that's not possible, limit any data access/modification to the bare minimum necessary to reproduce a PoC.
* Don't automate form submissions!
* If you don't follow these guidelines we will not award a bounty for the report.
* Be Patient - Give us a reasonable time to correct the issue before disclosure.
* We also expect you to comply with all applicable laws.
